lessonsIntro: Brighton Watersports runs mobile surf lessons, most of them at a spot in Shoreham, timed to the tide and with wetsuits included.

text: Brighton Watersports teaches surfing to all ages in groups, one-to-one or as progression sessions for people who already ride. Lessons are mobile but mostly happen in Shoreham, and the school tells you where to meet when you book. Wetsuits and buoyancy aids are provided, and you need to be able to swim. Bring your own board if you'd like to practise on it.

Sessions are planned around the tide, so you're asked to turn up on time. Surf on this stretch of the Sussex coast depends on Channel swell and wind, so flat days happen and the school picks the time and place to suit conditions. We couldn't confirm lifeguard cover or specific hazards at Shoreham Beach, so stick with the school while you're learning.

text: For learning, a large foam board is the easy option on small Channel waves. Brighton Watersports supplies wetsuits and buoyancy aids with lessons, and sells wetsuits and boards at its Brighton shop. Water temperatures on this coast run from about 6 to 8°C in late winter to 17 to 19°C in late summer, according to Wittering Surf Shop further west.

cards.label: Wetsuit

cards.text: Wittering Surf Shop, further west on the same coast, suggests a 3/2 or shorty July to October, 4/3 in May, June and November, and 5/4 with boots and gloves December to April.
